A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QIVD research, with readable text, tables, figures and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across renaming, reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR, streaming and offline question-answering evaluations, human comparisons, and VideoLLaMA fine-tuning experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds streaming-model training, timing and sampling experiments, judge comparisons, and dataset-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The original Whisper-Streaming pipeline remains, but v2 introduces Stream-Qwen-Omni (Section 5.2 and Appendix D.3). It processes one-second audiovisual chunks and learns to emit a listening token or an answer, training adapters and embeddings. This adds learned response timing and a new streaming inference procedure.

E1.justification: The core dataset remains 2,900 videos covering the same 13 categories. Appendix C.1 adds AVSD and Social-IQ to an empirical embedding-distribution comparison, without evaluating question answering on those datasets. The new facial-expression analysis uses 59 existing QIVD samples rather than newly collected coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds evaluated comparisons with VideoLLM-online, Flash-VStream, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B and Gemini-2.5-Flash. VideoLLM-online and Flash-VStream were only discussed in v1's related work. Appendix C.6 also introduces comparisons between alternative automatic judges and human ratings.

E3.justification: The main correctness judge changes from Llama3-8B to Qwen3-8B. v2 adds timestamp-source controls, separate early/late timing summaries, temporal sampling-window experiments, and a 300-sample human-rating study of GPT-4o answers. Newly specified settings for the retained VideoLLaMA experiment do not establish that its protocol changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained audio ablation and failure examples, v2 tests timestamp sources, temporal sampling windows, facial-expression performance, static versus temporal categories, judge sensitivity and metric correlations. It also analyzes ASR timing bias and cross-dataset embedding distributions. These substantially expand the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations for dataset characteristics; v2 additionally reports ASR and model-score standard deviations in Tables C.8-C.10. This extends descriptive variability reporting, but supplies no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests despite the 'Statistical Significance' heading.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new models and diagnostic experiments. Whisper-Streaming's reported timing MAE changes from 1.14 seconds to 0.83 seconds, and Stream-Qwen-Omni receives 0.52 seconds. Main correctness scores change under the new judge, including GPT-4o from 66.38% to 58.76%; this is not a same-protocol performance decline. Table C.7 largely preserves the earlier judge's results.

T1.justification: v1 describes timing error through aggregate MAE. v2 additionally defines signed error as the ASR timestamp minus the ground-truth timestamp in Figure B.3, supporting separate early and late error summaries. This is a limited mathematical-definition addition; no theoretical propositions or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: introduce the situated audiovisual benchmark, establish model-human performance gaps, demonstrate benefits from fine-tuning, and provide a streaming baseline. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly identifies small classes, controlled recording conditions and possible demographic biases as limitations. Other additions interpret premature ASR responses, dependence on audio after multimodal fine-tuning, and QIVD's separation from other datasets in embedding space. These materially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: v1 largely refers to checkpoint defaults for fine-tuning. v2 specifies deterministic fold construction, hardware, trainable modules, frame counts, precision, optimizer, learning-rate schedule and gradient accumulation, and documents Stream-Qwen-Omni's training format. It also replaces the competition-release notice with an explicit dataset-page address. These are substantial documentation additions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 Table 1 adds a structured comparison against 13 benchmarks, including AVSD, Social-IQ, LifeQA and TVQA. Appendix C.1 further positions QIVD through empirical comparisons with AVSD and Social-IQ. Together with references for newly evaluated models, this substantially expands research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most existing main-text prose and the main section sequence remain close to v1. Changes include standardizing the QIVD acronym, copyediting, moving the taxonomy to Appendix B.2, and regrouping supplementary material with a contents page. The extensive scientific additions do not amount to a wholesale rewrite of the original narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column conference layout, combines the streaming and offline comparison tables, redraws performance plots, and adds timing, distribution and architecture figures plus numerous analytical tables. Existing examples and refusal illustrations are relocated, while the combined judge-prompt table is split into two displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens investigation of the benchmark's central timing requirement through a learned streaming baseline, timestamp-source controls and timing diagnostics. Detailed training specifications address v1's reliance on unspecified defaults, while broader comparisons and explicit limitations improve interpretability. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: Table C.6 compares aggregate correctness rates rather than per-answer judge agreement, and Section 5.3 retains numerical statements that do not match the updated Figure 2.
